'''Miguel Calvo Rebollar''' (Soria, July 5, 1955) is a Spanish biochemist, mineralogist and professor at  Zaragoza University, Spain.

== Biography ==
Miguel Calvo Rebollar was born in [[Soria]], Spain. He studied chemistry at the Faculty of Sciences of the [[University of Zaragoza]]. He received his bachelor's degree in 1978 and his PhD in 1983. Her doctoral thesis, on the relationship between [[alpha-fetoprotein]] and the metabolism of [[Essential fatty acid|essential fatty acids]] during development, was supervised by Dr. Francisco Grande Covian.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Dialnet |url=https://dialnet.unirioja.es/servlet/tesis?codigo=206348}}</ref> Between 1985 and 1986, he conducted a postdoctoral research stay at the Institut de Recherches Scientifiques sur le Cancer, in [[Villejuif]] (París), in the group led by Dr. José Uriel to study the transport of the polyunsaturated fatty acids bound to proteins.<ref name=":0">{{Cite web |last=Wilson |first=Wendell E. |title=Mineralogical Record Biographical Archive |url=https://mineralogicalrecord.com/biographies_labels/calvomiguel/}}</ref>

In 1986, he was appointed as a senior lecturer in the Department of Food Science and Technology in the Zaragoza Faculty of Veterinary Science. That same year, as principal investigator, he formed in Zaragoza University the research group “Biochemistry of Milk Proteins” to study the biological properties of milk proteins, mainly those of [[lactoferrin]]<ref>{{Cite journal |last=Sánchez |first=Lourdes |last2=Calvo |first2=Miguel |last3=Brock |first3=Jeremy H. |title=Biological Role of Lactoferrin |journal=Archives of Disease in Childhood |volume=67 |pages=657-661 |doi=10.1136/adc.67.5.657 |archive-url=|url=https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC1793702/|pmc=1793702 }}</ref> and [[Β-Lactoglobulin|beta-lactoglobulin]]<ref>{{Cite journal |last=Pérez |first=Dolores |last2=Calvo |first2=Miguel |title=Interaction of beta-lactoglobulin with retinol and fatty acids and its role as a possible biological function for this protein. A review |journal=Journal of Dairy Science |volume=78 |pages=978-988}}</ref>. Also the effect of industrial processing on them, and particularly their possible usefulness in the preparation of infant foods. This group received the recognition from the Government of Aragon that same year, and has maintained it to this day.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Grupos investigación |url=https://www.unizar.es/institucion/historia/grupos-investigacion}}</ref>

In 1999 he received the Ordesa Prize from the Spanish Society of Pediatric Gastroenterology, Hepatology, and Nutrition for the study of the influence of thermal processing in infant foods.<ref>{{Cite book |last=Martín |first=Benjamín |title=Historia de la SEGHNP 1976-2012 |last2=Bautista |first2=Adolfo |publisher=Sociedad Española de Gastroenterología, Hepatología y Nutrición Pediátrica |year=2012 |page=209 |language=es |archive-url=|access-date=|url-status=live}}</ref> In his research work, he has supervised fifteen doctoral theses and published more than one hundred articles in scientific journals.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Universidad de Zaragoza. Miguel Calvo Rebollar |url=https://janovas.unizar.es/sideral/CV/miguel-calvo-rebollar}}</ref>

He has developed immunochemical analysis techniques and registered eight patents with the University of Zaragoza for methods to detect fraud in food production, as well as for detecting the presence of hidden allergens or genetically modified maize. He received the Idea-2001 Prize from Instituto Aragonés de Fomento for a spin-off project that gave rise to the company Zeu-Inmunotec (now Zeulab).<ref>{{Cite journal |last=Travesi |first=Begoña |date=June 3, 2002 |title=Una década de espíritu emprendedor |journal=Heraldo de Aragón |pages=3|publication-date=}}</ref> In 2006 he was appointed as a full professor at the Zaragoza University. Upon retiring, in 2025, he was named professor emeritus at the same university.

Miguel Calvo has been a mineral collector since a very young age and has maintained this activity throughout his life, developing it from both a scientific perspective and in the communication of the mineralogy of Spain and the history of mining. He has assembled a collection of around 10.000 mineral specimens.<ref name=":0" /><ref>{{Cite journal |last=Perla |first=Pilar |date=October 23, 2022 |title=Si los sabes interrogar, los minerales son parlanchines |url=https://www.heraldo.es/noticias/aragon/2022/10/22/si-los-sabes-interrogar-los-minerales-son-parlanchines-coleccion-miguel-calvo-1607439.html |journal=Heraldo de Aragón}}</ref>

This collection has served him for over twenty years of work in preparing the book Minerales y minas de España (''Minerals and Mines of Spain)'', published between 2003 and 2018 in nine volumes, totaling more than 5,000 pages. <ref>{{Cite journal |last=Petrov |first=Alfredo |title=Media Reviews. Minerales y Minas de España.Vol. 9: Silicatos [in Spanish] by Miguel Calvo |url=https://doi.org/10.1080/00357529.2019.1619142 |journal=Rocks & Minerals |volume=94 |issue=5 |page=477}}</ref>The work reviews approximately ten thousand Spanish mineral deposits, providing detailed geographic locations, the minerals found in each, and the characteristics of the specimens. For the most important mines, such as [[Almadén]], [[Las Médulas]], [[Rio Tinto (corporation)|Rio Tinto]], [[Sierra Menera]], [[Áliva]], and [[Remolinos]], historical details <ref>{{Cite journal |last=Callén |first=Joaquim |title=Topographic mineralogy and the book “Minerales y Minas de España”. |url=https://zenodo.org/records/3633613 |journal=Mineral Up |volume=5 |issue=3 |pages=74-78}}</ref>As a photographic complement, he published in collaboration with Christian Rewitzer ''Atlas de minerales de España—Atlas of Spanish Minerals'', a bilingual Spanish-English edition featuring 2,219 photos of 927 species.<ref>{{Cite journal |last=Pelckmans |first=Herwig |title=Atlas de Minerales de España/Atlas of Spanish Minerals |url=https://doi.org/10.1080/00357529.2023.2235994 |journal=Rocks & Minerals |volume=99 |issue=2 |page=189}}</ref>

As part of the European project MOMAr (Models of Management for Singular Rural Heritage), under Interreg Europe, funded by the European Union and coordinated by the Diputación Provincial de [[Zaragoza (Congress of Deputies constituency)|Zaragoza]] (Provincial Council of Zaragoza), he authored two books aimed at promoting the tourist use of the province’s mining heritage: one on former salt mines and saltworks and another on coal mines remains.<ref>{{Cite web |title=La Diputación de Zaragoza edita un libro con el que poner en valor el patrimonio cultural y natural de la sal en la provincia |url=https://www.dpz.es/noticias/la-diputacion-de-zaragoza-edita-un-libro-con-el-que-poner-en-valor-el-patrimonio-cultural-y-natural-de-la-sal-en-la-provincia}}</ref>

As a collaborator at the Museum of Natural Sciences of the University of Zaragoza, he organized, as curator, a temporary exhibition in 2019 to mark the International Year of the [[Periodic table|Periodic Table of Chemical Elements]], titled Construyendo la Tabla Periódica (Building the Periodic Table).<ref>{{Cite journal |last=de la Torre Egido |first=María del Carmen |year=2019 |title=Construyendo la Tabla Periódica |url=https://analesdequimica.es/index.php/AnalesQuimica/article/view/1360/1946 |journal=Anales de Química |volume=115 |pages=451}}</ref> He also curated the temporary exhibition Una pizca de sal (A Pinch of Salt), held from November 13, 2023, to February 3, 2024.<ref>{{Cite journal |last=Perla |first=María Pilar |date=December 17, 2023 |title=Los zaragozanos somos gente salada, y aquí está la explicación |url=https://www.heraldo.es/noticias/sociedad/2023/12/17/zaragozanos-somos-gente-salada-aqui-esta-explicacion-1697918.html |journal=Heraldo de Aragón}}</ref> Another exhibition he curated was Gemas de España. Tesoros de nuestra tierra (Gems of Spain, Treasures of Our Land), which took place from November 13, 2023, to February 3, 2026.<ref>{{Cite journal |last=Perla |first=Pilar |date=January 25, 2026 |title=De piedra a tesoro |journal=Heraldo Domingo-Heraldo de Aragón |issue=1088 |pages=1-3}}</ref> Each of these exhibitions was accompanied by the publication of a book with the same title. He has reviewed and reorganized the three historical mineral collections of the University of Zaragoza: the one from the Geology Section of the Faculty of Sciences, the Longinos Navás Collection located in the University’s Museum of Natural Sciences, and the collection that belonged to the geologist [[Lucas Mallada y Pueyo|Lucas Mallada]], preserved at the Faculty of Human Sciences and Education on the Huesca Campus.

He has published articles on the mineralogy of Spanish localities in Revista de Minerales (which has an English version, Mineral-Up), as well as in the Mineralogical Record, Lapis, Le Regne Mineral, Bocamina, Boletín Geológico y Minero, and others. He has also published papers on the history of mining. One of these, “Dinero no veían, solo fichas. El pago de salarios en las salitreras de Chile hasta 1925” (They Saw No Money, Only Tokens: Wage Payments in the Chilean Saltpeter Offices until 1925”, was awarded the  Francisco Javier Ayala Carcedo Prize.<ref>{{Cite journal |title=Entrega del VI premio Francisco Javier Ayala Carcedo |journal=De Re Metallica |volume=15 |pages=76-77}}</ref> As a science communicator, he has been an active critic of pseudoscience and food myths in the media.<ref>{{Cite journal |last=Calvo |first=Miguel |date=February 12, 2019 |title=Dos masdos suman cuatro |url=http://prensa.unizar.es/noticias/1902/190212_z1_L_21.pdf |journal=Heraldo de Aragón |page=21}}</ref>
